key_insight: Tensor-network decomposition turns a hard, entangled quantum wavepacket simulation into many smaller independent propagations that can run in parallel across mixed quantum-classical hardware.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers a practical route to scalable distributed quantum simulation, while native partial-entangling XX gates on trapped-ion hardware cut expected two-qubit gate infidelity by over 30% versus standard decompositions.
method: Represent multidimensional time evolution with a tensor network.
Lift the problem into an elevated Hilbert space where dynamics split into lower-dimensional tasks.
Execute the resulting subproblems asynchronously on heterogeneous quantum and classical systems using compiled XX(θ) circuits.
evidence_signal: On a trapped-ion quantum computer, the method reproduced vibrational spectra of a protonated water cluster within 4 cm^-1 of classical results.
watch_item: The workflow depends on successful tensor-network decomposition and hardware-specific circuit compilation, so performance may vary across devices and larger molecular systems.
paper_title: Tensor-Network-Based Distributed Quantum Dynamics on Independent Quantum Computers
